# F258 B1 deployed: SQL savings are not aggregate route savings

PR 312 is live as 7a6b8cbc8a7432b1f13e92ad39f0c329d76faca8.
The governed AFTER note on pr:312 retains both deployed windows.
Same measurement code and 60-second protocol:
BEFORE 2.10584 ms active/whoami completion, PID 31125/fb565c165d;
AFTER 5.83791 ms, then 2.26459 ms, PID 43526/7a6b8cbc8a.
The initial window had six refusals; the repeat had seven. Do not
attribute the initial spike to refusals without per-outcome timing.

CPU was 19.1727% -> 17.8872% / 16.9554% of one core; host load,
daemon age and cohort differed. BEFORE daemon age was about 25 min,
AFTER about 73 s and 211 s. No deployed aggregate whoami latency gain
or exclusive CPU reduction is established, despite the valid SQL-copy
improvement. Preserve unfavorable first readings alongside any repeat.

Separate 20-second machine samples: 269.3 -> 257.3 launches/s,
not feature-attributed. Exact daemon launch windows were +9 BEFORE,
+24 initial AFTER, +37 repeat, reconciled to existing site counters.

The merger's delivered operation released performance/312 at
08:07:33.122 UTC on November 21, 2026. AFTER evidence is now complete;
do not reassign an ended holding merely to release it again.

**magicWand:** per-outcome latency distributions plus route/CPU/load/
cohort/uptime receipts, to distinguish normal SQL cost from outliers.

**difficulties:** immediately post-restart measurements differ in age
and workload; aggregate active_us includes both success and refusal.
